title.narrative: Emergency response to address Acute Watery Diarrhea outbreak in White Nile State, Sudan.

description.narrative:
Durring the Month of May 2017, hundreds cases and several deaths related to Acute Watery Diarrhoea (AWD) has been reported in White Nile Sudan. The incidence of AWD are increasing with average of 60 patients daily reported cases from five localities Rabak, Kosti, Elgabalin, Elsalam and Elgitainah localities (Sudan -Ministry of health). There have been 11 cases of death confirmed so far.
The project seeks to reduce the susceptibility of getting AWD infection among the South Sudanese refugees and host communities.
The target affected population is 13,924 (6,266 children, 4,873 adult girls and women, 2,785 adult boys and men) in Elsalam locality and 41,840 (18,822 children,14644 girls and women, 8368 boys and men. CAFOD through its partner SIDO will facilitate this intervention in collaboration with ministry of health and relevant stake holders.
The project will: Train 80 community volunteers from the host communities in Acute watery Diarrhea prevention measurement and case findings to enable them to undertake mass and daily house to house awareness. The volunteers, also will be trained on house hold water chlorination to orient people to do chlorination at house hold level. In addition eight (8) microphones will be provided to mass campaigns. Moreover, 5000 pieces of soaps will be given to the vulnerable house holds for hand washing. The project will further provide (40) cartons of chlorine tabs 0.33g (1 carton capacity 10,000 tabs). This activity will be under direct supervision of ministry of health who will train the volunteers.
This is an emergency response and will be implemented in the next 30 days (June 2017) and close monitoring will be done in coordination with other stakeholders in White Nile.
